path_decisions.rationale: MTFAligner is dead code and ADX is computed but never consumed — regime detection is the natural bridge between MTF data availability and strategy consumption of that data
Regime should gate entry signals — currently all strategies use fixed strength (0.7-0.8) regardless of market regime, causing entries in unfavorable conditions that reduce win rate

YAML defines stop_loss_pct and stop_loss_atr_multiplier but these are NEVER wired into generate_signals() — trend_following and mean_reversion have zero stop-loss logic, exits rely solely on profit_target and trailing stop
Missing stop-loss means losing trades run until max_holding_bars timeout — this kills win rate. Tighter stops would increase win count but reduce profit factor; the tradeoff is unaddressed

evidence: quantflow/data/mtf_aligner.py:1-205 — complete MTFAligner class exists but grep confirms it is only referenced within its own file; no strategy or session imports it
quantflow/indicators/engine.py:117 — result['adx_14'] = trend.adx(high, low, close, 14) computes ADX but no strategy template reads adx_14 for regime filtering
quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:281-292 — trailing stop tracks highest CLOSE since entry, not highest HIGH — tighter than intended, causes premature exits
quantflow/strategy/templates/volatility_breakout.py:116-119 — on_bar() emits Direction.LONG when entry=True, even when short_count triggered the entry — short breakout signals lost
quantflow/strategy/templates/volatility_breakout.py:385-396 — same trailing-stop-tracks-close bug as trend_following, plus same short-direction gap

quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:107-122 — on_bar() emits Direction.LONG for entry and Direction.SHORT for exit, but exit signals should be Direction.FLAT to close positions, not SHORT to open new short positions
quantflow/strategy/engine.py:54-58 — RiskEngine and PositionSizer constructed with config.risk values but strategy_risk_budgets, strategy_win_rates never passed — confirms iter-1 finding
quantflow/strategy/engine.py:208 — size(signal, portfolio) called without strategy_win_rates — Kelly sizing defaults to win_rate=0.5 for all strategies
quantflow/signal/generator.py:54-88 — consolidate_signals() is defined but never called by TradingSession — conflicting signals from multiple strategies can open opposing positions

quantflow/config/strategies/trend_following.yaml:22-25 — defines stop_loss_pct: -0.05, stop_loss_atr_multiplier: 2.0, trailing_stop_atr_multiplier: 1.5 but trend_following.py __init__ never reads stop_loss_pct or stop_loss_atr_multiplier from params
quantflow/strategy/templates/_runtime.py:131-173 — profit_target_exit only checks close >= entry_price * (1+pct) — no short-direction handling, confirmed from iter-1
quantflow/strategy/templates/mean_reversion.py:138 — entries = (long_count >= min) | (short_count >= min) combines both directions into one boolean, losing directionality for profit_target_exit

quantflow/strategy/templates/funding_rate.py:78-80 — on_bar correctly determines Direction.LONG vs Direction.SHORT based on funding rate, but generate_signals (line 123) merges both into one entries boolean — profit_target_exit cannot differentiate
quantflow/common/models.py:77-82 — Position has no strategy_id field — risk budget cannot attribute positions to strategies, confirming iter-1 B5

candidate_solution.summary: 5 remaining bottleneck clusters: (1) MTFAligner+ADX dead code — no regime detection, (2) YAML stop_loss never wired — 0 stop-loss in trend_following/mean_reversion, (3) trailing stop tracks close not high — premature exits, (4) volatility_breakout loses short direction, (5) consolidate_signals never called — opposing positions possible

bottlenecks.title: MTFAligner is dead code — no strategy uses multi-timeframe confirmation
bottlenecks.description: quantflow/data/mtf_aligner.py provides a complete multi-timeframe alignment class (MTFAligner) with UTC-anchored rolling windows and forward-fill reindexing. However, grep confirms it is ONLY imported within its own file. No strategy template, no TradingSession, no signal generator references it. All 4 strategy templates operate on a single timeframe. This means trend_following enters on 1D data without checking whether the weekly trend aligns, and mean_reversion enters on 15m data without checking whether the 4H regime is ranging. Without higher-timeframe confirmation, ~30-40% of entries are counter-trend on the higher degree, directly reducing win rate.
bottlenecks.fix: 1) In TradingSession.on_bar(), after strategy generates signals but before _process_signal(), add MTFAligner.align() call to get primary/intermediate/minor data. 2) Add a regime_filter() method to each strategy that checks higher-TF alignment (e.g., trend_following only enters long when weekly MA trend is up). 3) Pass regime context to generate_signals() or on_bar() for filtering.

bottlenecks.title: ADX is computed but never consumed — no regime detection mechanism exists
bottlenecks.description: IndicatorEngine.batch_calculate() computes adx_14 (engine.py:117) and trend.adx() is a working implementation (trend.py:100-125). The ADX values > 25 = trending, < 20 = ranging. But no strategy template reads or uses adx_14 for regime detection or filtering. Trend_following enters trend positions regardless of whether ADX indicates a trending or ranging market. In ranging markets (ADX < 20), trend_following's MA crossover and MACD signals are noise, producing whipsaw entries with low win rate.
bottlenecks.fix: 1) Add adx_filter parameter to trend_following: only enter when adx > 25 (trending regime). 2) Add regime field to StrategyContext so strategies can query current regime. 3) In TradingSession, compute ADX on higher-TF data and pass regime to strategies.

bottlenecks.title: YAML stop_loss_pct is NEVER wired into any strategy — trend_following and mean_reversion have zero stop-loss
bottlenecks.description: trend_following.yaml:22 defines stop_loss_pct: -0.05 and stop_loss_atr_multiplier: 2.0. mean_reversion.yaml:17 defines stop_loss_pct: -0.03. But neither TrendFollowingStrategy.__init__() nor MeanReversionStrategy.__init__() reads stop_loss_pct from params. Neither generate_signals() nor _latest_signal() implements a stop-loss check. The only exit mechanisms are: (1) profit_target_exit (long-only, doesn't handle shorts), (2) trailing stop (tracks close not high), (3) max_holding_bars timeout. This means losing trades that gap against the position have NO hard stop — they hold until max_holding_bars (20 bars for trend, 10 for mean_rev), accumulating full drawdown. A trade entered at $100K with a -5% move ($95K) holds for 20 bars instead of stopping out at the 2-3 ATR level. This is the single biggest win rate killer: losing trades run to maximum loss while winning trades exit early at profit_target.
bottlenecks.fix: 1) Add stop_loss_pct param to all strategy __init__ methods. 2) In generate_signals(), add stop_exits: close < entry_price * (1 - stop_loss_pct) for longs, close > entry_price * (1 + stop_loss_pct) for shorts. 3) Add ATR-based stop: entry_price - atr * atr_multiplier for longs. 4) Include stop_exits in the final exits boolean: exits = exits | profit_exits | stop_exits | trailing_exits.

bottlenecks.title: Trailing stop tracks highest CLOSE instead of highest HIGH — stops are too tight
bottlenecks.description: In trend_following.py:281-292 and volatility_breakout.py:385-396, the trailing stop loop tracks `highest = max(close, previous_highest)`. For a long trailing stop, the correct tracking variable is the highest HIGH since entry, not highest close. Using close means intrabar highs that exceed the close are ignored, making the trailing stop trigger prematurely. For example, if a bar has high=$105K and close=$103K, the trailing stop uses $103K as the anchor, not $105K. With ATR_mult=3.0 and ATR=$2K, the trailing exit fires at $103K - $6K = $97K instead of $105K - $6K = $99K. This $2K difference causes valid pullback-then-continue trades to exit early, reducing win rate. Additionally, neither strategy tracks the LOWEST low for short-side trailing stops.
bottlenecks.fix: 1) Change the loop to track highest HIGH for long trailing stops: `highest = max(high.iloc[i], previous_highest)`. 2) Add lowest LOW tracking for short trailing stops: `lowest = min(low.iloc[i], previous_lowest)`. 3) Short trailing exit: close > lowest + atr * mult.

bottlenecks.title: volatility_breakout on_bar() always emits Direction.LONG — short breakout signals lost
bottlenecks.description: In volatility_breakout.py:114-130, when _latest_signal() returns entry=True, on_bar() always emits `Direction.LONG, strength=0.8` regardless of whether long_count or short_count triggered the entry. The _latest_signal() method combines both: `entry = long_count >= min or short_count >= min`, but returns only a boolean, losing direction. In generate_signals() (line 372), same issue: `entries = (long_count >= min) | (short_count >= min)` merges both directions. This means all short-side volatility breakout entries are silently converted to long entries, directly reducing win rate for the ~40-50% of breakouts that resolve downward.
bottlenecks.fix: 1) Change _latest_signal() to return (direction, entry, exit_) instead of (entry, exit_). 2) In generate_signals(), produce separate long_entries and short_entries. 3) Pass direction to profit_target_exit and trailing stop for direction-aware exit logic.

bottlenecks.title: consolidate_signals() never called — conflicting strategy signals can open opposing positions
bottlenecks.description: SignalGenerator.consolidate_signals() (generator.py:54-88) implements strength-weighted direction voting across multiple strategy signals for the same symbol. But TradingSession._process_signal() (engine.py:159-240) never calls consolidate_signals(). Each strategy's signal is processed independently through risk → sizing → execution. If trend_following emits LONG for BTC/USDT and mean_reversion simultaneously emits SHORT for BTC/USDT, both pass through the pipeline and both open positions — creating a self-hedging portfolio that earns no net return while paying fees. This is especially likely at trend reversals where trend signals lag and mean-reversion signals fire early.
bottlenecks.fix: 1) In TradingSession.on_bar(), after collecting all strategy signals, group by symbol and call consolidate_signals() for symbols with multiple signals. 2) Only process the consolidated signal through _process_signal(). 3) For single-strategy signals, pass through directly.

bottlenecks.title: All strategies use hardcoded signal strength — no regime-adaptive strength
bottlenecks.description: trend_following.on_bar() emits strength=0.8 (line 109) and strength=0.5 (line 120). mean_reversion.on_bar() emits strength=0.7 (line 69). volatility_breakout.on_bar() emits strength=0.8 (line 119). These are constant regardless of signal quality. A trend_following entry where all 4 conditions are met (count=4) gets the same strength as an entry where only min_conditions=4 are met (i.e., exactly 4 of 4). Multi-condition strategies should scale strength with condition count: strength = min_conditions/total_conditions * base_strength. Additionally, signal strength should be reduced in unfavorable regimes (low ADX). This causes PositionSizer to allocate the same dollar amount to both high-quality and marginal signals, diluting win rate.
bottlenecks.fix: 1) In generate_signals(), compute strength based on condition_count / total_conditions. 2) In on_bar(), pass computed strength to emit_signal() instead of hardcoded value. 3) Multiply strength by regime factor (e.g., ADX/50 for trending, 1-ADX/50 for ranging).

bottlenecks.title: trend_following on_bar() exit signal uses Direction.SHORT — opens new short instead of closing long
bottlenecks.description: trend_following.py:118-122 emits `Direction.SHORT, strength=0.5` for exit signals. In TradingSession._process_signal() (engine.py:218), a SHORT direction signal creates a SELL order: `side = OrderSide.BUY if signal.direction.value > 0 else OrderSide.SELL`. This SELL order creates a new short position or adds to an existing short, rather than closing the existing long position. The correct exit signal should be Direction.FLAT (which SignalGenerator.generate_signal() treats as None at generator.py:43) or a separate close signal. This causes exit signals to open new positions in the opposite direction instead of closing the existing one, increasing exposure and reducing win rate through unintended doubled positions.
bottlenecks.fix: 1) Change exit signal emission to use Direction.FLAT or a dedicated close signal. 2) In _process_signal(), add logic to check if an opposing signal should close an existing position rather than open a new one. 3) Consider a position management layer that maps exit signals to close orders.

calibration_gaps.issue: Code defaults to 3.0 ATR (very wide) but YAML specifies 1.5. Since YAML is never wired, code uses 3.0. A 3.0 ATR trailing stop on BTC with ATR=$2000 means $6000 trailing distance — a winning trade can give back $6000 before stopping out. 1.5 ATR = $3000 is much tighter. Both values should be validated against backtest but the code/YAML mismatch is a critical wiring bug.

YAML defines stop_loss_atr_multiplier: 2.0 but trend_following.py never reads this param. A 2.0 ATR stop would mean $4000 initial stop loss on BTC. Since this is never implemented, the effective stop is max_holding_bars=20 which could result in 5-10% drawdowns instead of the intended 2-4%.

Code defaults to 3% but YAML specifies 5%. Since YAML is never wired into __init__, code uses 3%. For mean reversion, 3% is very tight — many reversals reach 3% but then continue to 5-8%. Exiting at 3% leaves significant profit on the table.

Code defaults to 2.5 but YAML specifies 2.0. Since YAML is never wired, code uses 2.5. Additionally, the trailing stop tracks close not high, making effective trailing distance even wider than intended.

interaction_effects.issue: Without stop-loss, the exit asymmetry is extreme: winning trades exit at profit_target (e.g., 10%) but losing trades run to max_holding_bars (potentially -15% to -25%). This asymmetric exit profile means one losing trade can wipe out 2-3 winning trades' profits. The profit_factor is depressed because losses accumulate to maximum while profits are capped early.

For short positions, neither trend_following nor volatility_breakout tracks the lowest low. The trailing stop uses `close < highest - atr*mult` which is wrong for shorts — it should be `close > lowest + atr*mult`. This means short-side trailing stops never fire correctly, and short winning trades hold until max_holding_bars or another exit triggers. Combined with profit_target_exit being long-only, short-side win rate is severely depressed.

interaction_effects.pair: hardcoded strength + Kelly sizing with default win_rate=0.5
interaction_effects.issue: PositionSizer.size() at engine.py:208 uses default win_rate=0.5 (because strategy_win_rates is never passed). With hardcoded strength=0.8 and win_rate=0.5, raw_kelly = (0.5*2.0 - 0.5)/2.0 = 0.25, then size = total_value * 0.5 * 0.25 * 0.8 = 10% of portfolio per trade. All strategies get the same sizing regardless of their actual win rate, so a strategy with 55% win rate is sized identically to one with 45% win rate — no differentiation.

missing_mechanisms.description: MTFAligner exists but is dead code. No strategy uses higher-timeframe trend confirmation. Trend_following on 1D data should only enter long when weekly trend is up; mean_reversion on 15m should only enter when 4H is ranging (low ADX). This would filter ~30% of counter-trend entries.

YAML defines stop_loss_pct for all strategies but it is NEVER implemented in generate_signals(). No hard stop exists for trend_following or mean_reversion. A proper stop-loss would cap losing trades at 2-3 ATR or 3-5% instead of letting them run to max_holding_bars timeout at potentially 15-25% loss.

SignalGenerator.consolidate_signals() exists but is never called by TradingSession. When multiple strategies emit conflicting signals for the same symbol, both pass through and both open positions, creating self-hedging portfolios.

priority_ranking.reason: No stop-loss means losing trades run to maximum loss — this is the single biggest win rate killer. Every other exit optimization is irrelevant if losses are uncapped.

No MTF confirmation means ~30% of entries are counter-trend on the higher degree. Adding weekly trend filter for trend_following and 4H regime filter for mean_reversion would filter the worst entries.
Trailing stop tracks close instead of high — causes premature exits on valid pullbacks. Fix is simple (use high column) and would immediately improve trailing stop effectiveness.
volatility_breakout loses short direction — all short breakouts become long entries. This directly kills short-side win rate for the volatility strategy.
ADX exists but never used for regime filtering — close cousin to C1 but specifically about trend vs ranging discrimination.
Conflicting strategy signals create self-hedging positions — important for multi-strategy portfolios but lower impact for single-strategy runs.
Exit signals use Direction.SHORT instead of Direction.FLAT — opens new positions instead of closing. High impact but only affects trend_following on_bar path.
Hardcoded signal strength means no quality discrimination — moderate impact on Kelly sizing but lower than structural bugs.

notes: Key insight: YAML wiring is a systemic problem across ALL strategies. Every YAML config defines stop_loss_pct, take_profit_pct, trailing_stop_atr_multiplier but strategy __init__ only reads params that match the code default names, which differ from YAML names. For example, YAML uses 'trailing_stop_atr_multiplier' but code uses 'trailing_stop_atr_mult'. YAML uses 'stop_loss_atr_multiplier' but code has no such param at all. This naming mismatch means YAML calibration values are silently ignored even if the wiring code were added.
